correctness.rationale: PASS. The graph and cut-complex definitions are explicit. Exhaustive enumeration finds exactly \(32\) disconnected four-sets and \(8\) disconnected five-sets, with face vectors \((8,28,56,32)\) and \((8,12,8)\). The complete two-skeleton makes \(\Delta_4(Q_3)\) simply connected. Exact boundary ranks are \((7,21,32)\); a maximal \(\partial_3\) minor has determinant \(-1\), so the middle homology is integrally \(\mathbb Z^3\) with no hidden torsion. Hurewicz plus homological Whitehead gives \(\bigvee^3S^2\). At level five the facets are exactly the two parity tetrahedral boundaries, and both filling tetrahedra are actual level-four simplices, yielding a genuine null-homotopy of the inclusion. The included verifier replays every finite claim.
risks: The finite computations are exact for this eight-vertex graph only; the final homotopy equivalence uses standard general topology rather than an explicit collapse.

value.rationale: PASS. The three-cube is a canonical graph and the cut complexes form a natural nested filtration introduced for topological study. The result determines two adjacent upper levels completely and, beyond Betti numbers, determines the actual inclusion up to null-homotopy: the two \(S^2\) components at level five die when passing to level four even though level four has three new \(H_2\) generators. This gives a compact exact benchmark for future hypercube and grid cut-complex investigations rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
risks: The value is as a canonical exact benchmark and map-level example; no general hypercube family theorem or downstream application is claimed.
